title: Sowing pea shoots
subtitle: How to pre-soak and sow a pea shoot tray, from seed to the start of blackout
excerpt: Pea shoots need an 8 to 12 hour pre-soak before sowing. The large seeds swell in water, absorb the germination trigger, then go into a deep tray in a dense single layer. Sowing pea shoots takes five minutes plus the overnight soak.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: Soaking large, hard-coated seeds (peas, sunflowers, beans) in room-temperature water for 6 to 12 hours before sowing. The water penetrates the seed coat, triggers the germination signal, and dramatically reduces the time to the first visible shoot.

The period immediately after sowing when a second tray is stacked on top, blocking light from the sown tray. In darkness, germinating seeds direct energy into pushing the shoot upward rather than greening. The shoots reach 3 to 4 cm before the cover is removed and the tray is moved to light.

content.text: Sowing pea shoots has one extra step compared to small-seed crops: the pea seed needs an 8 to 12 hour pre-soak before it goes into the tray. Set up the soak the evening before sowing day. The sowing itself is quick once the soaked seeds are ready.

One 25 cm × 25 cm deep growing tray (at least 4 cm deep; pea roots are longer than brassica roots). A second tray for the blackout cover. Seed compost. Pea seed: 80 to 100 g per tray. A bowl for soaking. A flat weight (250 to 500 g) for the blackout cover.
80 to 100 g of pea seed in a bowl of room-temperature water. Use enough water to keep the seeds submerged; they will absorb a significant amount overnight. Soak for 8 to 12 hours.

Step 1: drain and rinse the soaked seeds. The water will be slightly cloudy from surface sugars; drain it off and rinse the seeds under cold running water. The seeds should be visibly swollen and some may already show a white root tip.

Step 2: fill the tray with pre-dampened seed compost, leaving 2 cm from the rim. A deeper tray (4 cm or more) gives the pea root system room to develop; shallow trays work but produce slightly shorter and coarser shoots.

Step 3: spread the soaked seeds in a dense single layer across the surface of the medium. Pea seeds are large enough to self-support. Do not stack seeds on top of each other; a single layer maximises germination and airflow.
Step 4: press gently down on the layer of seeds to ensure good contact with the medium beneath.

: stack a second tray directly on top and add a flat weight. Pea seeds push upward forcefully; a weight ensures they push against resistance and keep good contact with the medium. Leave in darkness for three days before checking.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common sowing-stage problems with pea shoots.

items.symptom: Mould on some seeds within the first two days
items.cause: Seeds with low viability that fail to germinate, providing a food source for mould.
items.fix: Rinse the soaked seeds more thoroughly before sowing. Pick out any seeds that look shrivelled or discoloured before spreading them in the tray. Use fresh seed.

items.symptom: Cover lifts up during the blackout phase
items.cause: The pea seeds push up forcefully as they germinate.
items.fix: Use a heavier weight on top. If the cover is lifting too easily, add a full water bottle (about 500 g) on top.

items.symptom: Seeds dry out in the tray despite the pre-soak
items.cause: Pre-dampened medium was too dry, or room is very warm.
items.fix: Ensure the compost is thoroughly pre-dampened before filling. Bottom-water the tray once on day 1 or 2 if the medium feels dry through the drainage holes.
